item.tests: Tests turning an attached product photo into one coherent 15-second vertical ad while preserving product identity.

answer_sheet.Product reference: The matte black bottle in product-bottle.jpg; preserve its shape, finish and lid.
answer_sheet.Style and setting: Clean studio look with moving close-ups; background and colours are your call.
answer_sheet.Text: Start with “Your everyday bottle” and end with “Shop now”; no invented brand or product claims.
answer_sheet.Format and duration: One 15-second 9:16 video; free-tier resolution is fine.

must_haves: One playable 9:16 ad runs for approximately 15 seconds, not just a single clip of 10 seconds or less.
The featured product matches the supplied matte black bottle, including its silhouette and lid.
The ad includes multiple moving product views or close-ups in a clean studio setting.
The opening reads exactly “Your everyday bottle” and the ending reads exactly “Shop now”.
Mellow music is audible and there is no spoken voice.

turns.text: Make a 15-second vertical 9:16 ad for the bottle in this pic. Use a clean studio look, a few moving close-ups, mellow music, and no talking. Start with “Your everyday bottle” and end with “Shop now”. Keep the bottle looking like mine. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any generation or spent credits.** I can use your attached photo as the bottle reference.

For your brief, I’d plan:
- **0–3s:** full bottle on a clean studio background — “Your everyday bottle”
- **3–11s:** gentle moving close-ups of the loop cap and matte-black finish
- **11–15s:** full-bottle closing shot — “Shop now”
- Mellow instrumental music, no voice.

### Cost and cheaper options
I **can’t verify your balance or get an exact video-credit quote with the connected tools**, so I won’t submit a generation and risk an unexpected charge.

| Option | Cost I can verify |
|---|---|
| **15-second AI video, 480p** using a free-plan-compatible model | Video cost unavailable here; I can’t quote a reliable total |
| **5-second AI video, 480p**, one slow camera move | A lower-cost candidate, but exact credits still need verification |
| **Studio-style still image**, then animate it in a conventional editor | Image edit starts at **5 credits** with Flux 2 Klein at 640px; no AI-video credits needed |
| **Animate the original photo with crops/zooms in an editor** | **0 Magic Hour generation credits**; editing/music licensing costs depend on your editor |

**My recommendation:** use a conventional editor for a 15-second vertical ad with slow pans, close-up crops, exact text overlays, and licensed mellow music. That preserves your actual bottle most faithfully and avoids paying for AI video. A studio-background image edit would be optional.

Two important limitations:
- AI video can alter the bottle’s shape or cap; exact text is more reliable as an editing overlay.
- Magic Hour’s workflow guidance says **commercial use requires a paid subscription, credit-pack purchase, or another agreed paid arrangement**—so free generation alone shouldn’t be assumed cleared for a published ad.

Would you prefer a **zero-generation-credit editing recipe**, or to **check Magic Hour’s quote and commercial-use eligibility before generating**?
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that — the zero-generation-credit editing recipe.

turns.agent:
## Zero-generation-credit editing recipe

Use **CapCut, Canva, DaVinci Resolve, or another editor** with your original photo. This uses **0 Magic Hour credits**, preserves your actual bottle, and requires no AI generation.

### 1. Set up the project
- **Canvas:** vertical 9:16, 1080 × 1920
- **Length:** 15 seconds
- **Background:** warm off-white or pale gray
- Import your bottle photo.

For the clean studio look, use a **manual cutout/background-removal feature only if it’s free in your editor**. Keep the loop opening transparent and preserve the cap and bottle edges. Place the cutout centrally with a subtle shadow beneath it.

If free background removal isn’t available, use the original photo with the fallback below.

### 2. Build this timeline

| Time | Picture and movement | Text |
|---|---|---|
| **0–3s** | Full bottle, centered with generous space. Slowly enlarge from 100% to 105%. | **Your everyday bottle** |
| **3–6.5s** | Cut to the cap and loop. Use a gentle sideways pan, keeping the cap fully visible. | None |
| **6.5–10s** | Close-up of the matte-black body. Slowly pan vertically to show its finish. | None |
| **10–12s** | Return to the full bottle with a subtle zoom out. | None |
| **12–15s** | Hold the full bottle, centered and still. | **Shop now** |

**Editing tip:** duplicate the same photo/cutout for each shot, then change its crop and position. Use keyframes for movement. Keep transitions simple—straight cuts or short dissolves.

### 3. Style the text
- Simple sans-serif, such as **Inter** or **Montserrat**
- Dark charcoal on the pale background
- Opening line near the top; closing line beneath the bottle
- Keep text comfortably away from the frame edges and social-app controls
- Fade each caption in and out over about **0.25 seconds**

### 4. Add music
Choose a **15-second instrumental** with mellow keys, soft guitar, or a light ambient beat—**no vocals**.

Use a track whose license explicitly permits **commercial advertising on your intended platform**. “Free” or “royalty-free” alone doesn’t guarantee that permission. Add a short fade-in and a **one-second fade-out**.

### 5. Export
- **MP4 / H.264**
- **1080 × 1920**, 30 fps
- Use **720 × 1280** for a smaller file; it won’t change the zero-credit cost.

### No-cutout fallback
Keep the original photo as a centered square panel on a pale vertical canvas. Put the opening and closing text in the empty space above or below it. Use cropped duplicates for the close-ups. This won’t look fully studio-shot, but it avoids cutout fees and preserves the bottle exactly.

**Quality note:** your source is 512 × 512, so keep close-ups moderate. Extreme zooms will look soft; a larger export won’t add detail.
